## 1. Native ports and the controller we build

There are two colocated periodic native rings with N sites. Their native
carrier channels remain separate. Visible x_1,x_2 are signed harmonic densities
with zero sum, not exclusion occupations. Put `(B_N j)_i=j_(i-1)-j_i` and

    B=diag(B_N,B_N), R=diag(r_1 I_N,r_2 I_N),
    0<r_-<=r_1,r_2<=r_+.

The native resistances may be unknown frozen values. Actual current response,
load and temperature-one noise are

    dx=Bv dt,
    tau dv=-(B^*x+g_N q)dt-Rv dt+f_N(t)dt+sqrt(2R)dW.       (1)

Here tau>0 is fixed. The reciprocal local tap into q and its reaction -g_N q
are supplied matched ports. They do not follow from equilibrium weights.
W has independent components in the two native systems.

Build the local 3N-by-2N matrix

    A = [[ B_N,     0 ],
         [   0,  -B_N ],
         [ I_N,   I_N ]].                                 (2)

The first two row blocks connect neighbors along each memory ring; the last
connects colocated cells across rings. Thus range and degree are bounded.
This is a ladder incidence after reversing the second ring's memory polarity:

    ker A=span{h_N}, h_N=(1_N,-1_N)/sqrt(2N), B h_N=0.       (3)

Run the actual controller

    dq=(g_N v-a A^*p)dt,
    dp=(a A q-gamma A A^*p)dt+sqrt(2gamma)A dV,              (4)

with fixed a>0, gamma>=0 and independent same-temperature local bath V.
Relative-momentum damping is structural. Grounded loss is a different port.
The actual native current is `J_a,tot=sum_i int v_(a,i)dt`, counting all
reaction motion. Apparatus transport is a separate declared channel.

Write kappa_N=g_N^2 and assume

    kappa_N ->0,       N^2 kappa_N ->infinity.               (5)

Every local native/wave coefficient is bounded; the tap becomes weak and pays
accuracy/compliance and range. Gaussian coordinates are not a hard-capacity
apparatus. Native current has finite response tau/r_a, while the mathematical
voltage baths use white noise. The separate finite-duration rotation program
supplies a different isolated bath interface; it is not composed through an
unknown resistor by inference.

## 3. Both nonflat density histories remain ordinary and independent

Let F=B A^dagger, with the Moore--Penrose inverse used only in the proof.
Since ker A is contained in ker B, F A=B. At Fourier eigenvalue ell of B_N^*B_N,
A^*A has eigenvalues ell+2 on the common-ring combination and ell on the
difference combination. Consequently

    ||F||<=1,       F A A^* F^*=BB^*.                      (7)

No nonlocal F sensor is used by the apparatus. Combining actual equations gives

    R_x dx=-BB^*x dt-tau d(Bv)-(g_N/a)F dp
            -(g_N gamma/a)F AA^*p dt
            +sqrt(2R_x)B dW+(g_N/a)sqrt(2gamma)B dV,        (8)

where R_x has the same two constant blocks as R. Couple reference densities to
the same mathematical W and initial x_N^0:

    dy_a=-(1/r_a)B_N B_N^*y_a dt+sqrt(2/r_a)B_N dW_a.       (9)

These reference laws are independent. This proof coupling does not physically
branch one specimen. For a unit Fourier vector f in one density ring, put
w=F^*f. Then ||w||<=1 and w^*(gamma AA^*)w=gamma ell. The actual stationary
forward/backward martingale identity gives

    E |int_0^t <gamma AA^*w,p_s>ds|^2<=2t gamma ell.        (10)

Indeed, for h=<w,p> its symmetric generator is Sh=-<gamma AA^*w,p>.
The forward and adjoint backward martingales sum to twice the displayed
integral, and each has expected square 2t gamma ell. Cauchy--Schwarz proves
(10), without mixing. Conditioning deterministic initial x reduces the centered
covariance of this linear path functional.

The Fourier difference from (9) obeys a scalar Volterra equation with decay
ell/r_a. The source in (8) consists of two endpoint momenta, (10), and the
controller martingale. Uniformly for physical t<=N^2T its centered second moment
is bounded by

    C_T[ell+kappa_N(1+N^2 ell)].                            (11)

The Volterra resolvent has L1 norm at most one. Thus (11), up to factor four,
bounds the difference at each time and vanishes for every fixed macroscopic
Fourier index. For the deterministic mean, energy contraction tested by
f/sqrt(N) bounds the native endpoint by O(sqrt(ell)), the auxiliary endpoint by
O(g_N), and the loss integral by C_T g_N N sqrt(ell). They vanish too.

The native matrix impedance has real part at least r_-I, giving the thermal
spectrum S_v=2 Re Y <=(2/r_-)I and the increment bound

    E |<f,x_t-x_s>|^2 <=(2 ell/r_-)|t-s|.                  (12)

Gaussian moments, Sobolev summation, and compact embedding give joint path
tightness on the macroscopic clock in C([0,T],H^(-s)), s>3/2. Conditioning only
reduces covariance. Energy/Fourier tails treat smooth nonflat means. Together
with (11), the coupled centered difference converges to zero in this path space.
For a tight Gaussian sequence converging to zero, a common Fernique bound
makes its expected norm and weak variance tend to zero. Borell's inequality
therefore makes the macroscopic difference (divided by sqrt(N)) superexponentially
small at speed N. This step is specific to the exact Gaussian path laws.

Thus the two complete density histories are exponentially equivalent to
independent native heat histories, with respective deterministic receivers

    partial_t rho_a=(1/r_a)partial_x^2 rho_a.               (13)

Their two limiting centered fluctuation fields are independent conservative OU
fields, started at zero for the specified deterministic visible initializer.

## 5. Full joint action and the independent-density consequence

Define empirical density and integrated-current fields

    rho_(a,N)=N^(-1)sum_i x_(a,i)(N^2t)delta_(i/N),
    W_(a,N)=N^(-2)sum_i J_(a,i)(N^2t)delta_(i/N).

Exact continuity reconstructs each nonconstant current mode from the density
change by a discrete inverse gradient. The inverse multipliers converge in
the weak Sobolev path topology. Sections 3-4 give the joint Gaussian fluctuation
limit and exponential tightness. The Gaussian LDP (or quadratic finite-projection
moment-generating functions plus exponential tightness) supplies the speed-N
good rate

    I(rho_1,rho_2,j_1,j_2)
       =sum_(a=1,2)(r_a/4) int_0^T int_0^1
                       [j_a+(1/r_a)partial_x rho_a]^2 dxdt, (18)

on

    partial_t rho_a+partial_x j_a=0,
    rho_a(0)=rho_(a,0),
    integral j_1(t,x)dx=integral j_2(t,x)dx  a.e. t,        (19)

and infinity otherwise. W_a(t)=int_0^t j_a(s)ds is the measured current path.
Finite action is the weak controlled-PDE/Cameron--Martin image of an L2
control, rather than a formula defined only on smooth paths.

Indeed, write j_a=j_a^perp+I(t), with zero-mean j_a^perp. The independent density
costs are the two ordinary native ones. The common Brownian mode contributes
((r_1+r_2)/4)int I^2dt by (16), exactly giving (18). Contracting over current
sets I=0 and leaves the sum of the independent heat density actions. The local
operation thus changes joint transport without locking spatial density profiles,
including their rare histories at this Gaussian precision objective.

# Carry the out-of-band supplier into the measurement bound

30 October 2026. Root correction after the actual-file receiving review by the
existing record-geometry role. Read this with `LOCAL_PASSIVE_LAW_REALIZATION.md`;
the original reviewed version is preserved unchanged.

The original native bounds (2) are only in the declared band. The measurement
bound (18) is valid as printed only if `A_out=0`, or if the **global coercivity
alternative** from Section 5 is actually warranted outside the band as well.
Section 6's phrase "under the bounds above" did not carry that condition
explicitly enough. No out-of-band spectrum is certified by in-band passivity
and norm bounds alone.

With a separately warranted outside-band envelope

    ||S_v(omega)-S_*(omega)|| <= E_out(omega),

the correct covariance error is instead

    delta_Sigma <= 2T Delta A_in
       + int_outside ||F(omega)||_op^2 E_out(omega) d omega/(2pi).

Then the same finite-record Gaussian KL/TV calculation applies if the resulting
relative covariance error is below one. Without such a supplier, (18)-(19)
are asserted only for an exactly in-band observation. A real finite-duration
filter generally has spectral leakage; its acquisition and noise objective
must therefore carry the extra information. A passive narrow RLC resonance
outside the measured band is a concrete reason an uncontrolled extrapolation
can fail. No fixed finite calibration grid rules it out by itself.

In the scaling statement after (13), a is fixed and strictly positive as in
Section 2, or has a warranted uniform positive lower bound. An upper bound on
a alone is insufficient if a is allowed to vary with N. With a tending to zero,
both the allowed observation band and Delta must be evaluated from (10)-(11)
without the stated fixed-a simplification.

These changes do not alter the Schur bound, exact response/noise identity,
actual local operation, or the singular-record warning. They restrict the
information that can support a finite-precision measurement claim.

## 3. Required correction: a leaking filter needs an out-of-band supplier

The in-band hypotheses (2) do not imply equation (18) when `A_out>0`. The coefficient `4T/r_-` in that equation requires the extra global-coercivity alternative explicitly stated in Section 5, or another warranted bound on the actual out-of-band spectral difference. This is not just a technical issue concerning very high frequencies.

Here is an analytic passive counterexample to the unqualified extrapolation. Embed a scalar P current into a two-current system with `A=(0,1)`, `B=0`, and a positive constant resistance on the Q current. On P choose

\[
R_P(z)=\delta+\frac{r_0}{1+\tau z}+\mathcal L z,
\qquad
\mathcal L=\frac{r_0\tau}{1+\omega_0^2\tau^2}
             +\frac{\kappa}{\omega_0^2},
\]

where all parameters are positive and `omega_0` lies outside the measured band. This is a causal positive-real impedance. At `omega_0`, the imaginary part of `R_P(i omega)+kappa/(i omega)` cancels exactly, and

\[
\Re Y_P(i\omega_0)
=\frac{1}{\delta+r_0/(1+\omega_0^2\tau^2)}.
\]

For example fix `Omega=1/10`, `tau=10`, `r_0=kappa=a=lambda=1`, take `omega_0>=1`, and let `0<delta<=0.01`. The in-band real-part bound `r_-=1/2` and norm bound `r_+=1.2` hold uniformly, and both conditions (10) hold. As `omega_0` grows and delta decreases, the outside-band current spectrum becomes arbitrarily large. The ideal P current is zero. A normalized observation filter concentrated near that outside resonance violates the proposed fixed outside-band coefficient. Strictly positive delta makes the passive closed-loop scalar realization damped; the example does not rely on an excluded visible undamped mode.

The root correction gives precisely the needed repair:

\[
\delta_\Sigma\le 2T\Delta A_{\rm in}
+\int_{\rm outside}\|F(\omega)\|_{\rm op}^2
 E_{\rm out}(\omega)\,\frac{d\omega}{2\pi},
\]

with an actually warranted envelope `E_out`, or `A_out=0`. Under global coercivity, the printed constant `4T/r_-` follows because each admittance has norm at most `1/r_-`. The correction explicitly notes the spectral leakage of a real finite-duration filter and does not infer an envelope from a finite calibration grid. **This correction is accepted.**

After a valid covariance error has been supplied, the Gaussian KL direction and constants in (19) are correct. If the ideal measured covariance is `Sigma_*>=sigma^2 I`, write

\[
E=\Sigma_*^{-1/2}(\Sigma-\Sigma_*)\Sigma_*^{-1/2}.

Then `||E||<=a_0`, and the actual-to-ideal covariance contribution is
`(1/2) sum_j [u_j-log(1+u_j)]`. For `|u_j|<=a_0<1`, this is at most `d a_0^2/[4(1-a_0)]`; the mean contribution is bounded by `||delta_mu||^2/(2 sigma^2)`. Pinsker gives the stated TV estimate.

This is the law of the supplied finite linear measurement vector with its actual independent sensor noise. It is not an estimate for noiseless full trajectories. If a nontrivial P component is observed without noise, the ideal component is identically zero while the actual finite-kappa thermal Gaussian component can have nonzero variance. Their laws are then singular, despite small in-band operator error. The root text correctly uses this as a possibility, not as an assertion about every filter or a zero-temperature experiment.

Conditional application with a retained old record is valid when every conditional port, preparation, and future source law satisfies the same hypotheses. ## 2. An exact response-and-noise criterion

At a frozen native state, write the unconstrained infinitesimal current as

    dJ=b dt+sqrt(2M)dW.

The ideal force-only reciprocal constraint adds the Lagrange force H dLambda
before multiplication by M. Eliminating dLambda from H* dJ=0 gives

    T_M=I-MH G^(-1)H*,
    dJ_c=T_M b dt+T_M sqrt(2M)dW,
    M_c=T_M M T_M*=M-MH G^(-1)H*M.                         (1)

For a physical force b=Mf, response is M_c f and covariance is 2M_c dt.
This native metric projection generally differs from Q M Q. The density
covariance removed by it is exactly

    2B(M-M_c)B*=2(BMH)G^(-1)(BMH)*.                        (2)

Consequently these statements are equivalent: density noise covariance is
unchanged; B M_c f=B M f for every force f; and BMH=0. The first follows
because (2) is L L* for L=sqrt(2)BMH G^(-1/2). The response difference is
BMH G^(-1)H*M; multiplication on the right by H proves its converse.

Topology alone, BH=0, is insufficient. The protected directions must remain
divergence free after multiplication by the actual mobility. In the accepted
two-ring theorem M is a spatially constant scalar on each ring, so BMH=0
even when the unknown scalars differ. Spatially varying mobility usually

# Volume-uniform imaginary-time product-formula control

**Status (2026-10-29): proved below; independently audited.** This is an elementary derivation, not a claim of literature novelty. It establishes the physical approximation obligation only. It does not establish any counting-algorithm or bit-complexity claim.

## Statement

Let `H = sum_a h_a` act on `n` finite-dimensional spins. Assume:

* every `h_a` is Hermitian and supported on at most `k >= 1` sites;
* `||h_a|| <= J`;
* each site occurs in at most `D` terms, with `k,D,J` independent of `n`.

Extract scalar/empty-support terms and handle their exponential exactly. Then the number `m` of remaining terms is at most `nD`. Local spin dimensions may be arbitrary for the operator statement, but a fixed bound `d` is used for the ground-energy consequence.

Color the term-overlap graph using `q <= k(D-1)+1` colors. Each layer `H_j` is a sum of terms with pairwise disjoint supports. Put

\[
E_j(t)=e^{-tH_j/2},\quad Q(t)=E_q(t)\cdots E_1(t),\quad P(t)=Q(t)^\dagger Q(t),
\]

and

\[
M=\sum_{\ell=1}^{q}k^\ell,\qquad x=JM\delta.
\]

Thus `P` is a positive, symmetric, local-factor product; explicitly it has the palindromic sequence `E_1 ... E_q E_q ... E_1` and is a second-order formula. For every finite `n` and every `delta >= 0`,

\[
\boxed{\|\log P(\delta)+\delta H\|
\le {2m\over M}\,[\sinh(JM\delta)-JM\delta].} \tag{1}
\]

Consequently, for every `beta > 0` and positive integer `r`,

\[
\boxed{
{1\over n}\left|\log\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H}
-\log\operatorname{Tr}P(\beta/r)^r\right|
\le {2Dr\over M}\,[\sinh(x)-x]
\le {D J^3 M^2 e^x\over3}\,{\beta^3\over r^2},
\quad x={JM\beta\over r}.} \tag{2}
\]

There is no restriction on the interaction graph other than the incidence bound: expanders are allowed. No positivity of individual matrix entries, stoquasticity, geometric block cutting, clustering, gap, high-temperature restriction on `beta`, or thermodynamic limit is used.

For target normalized log-partition error `eta`, it suffices to choose

\[
r\ge\max\left\{JM\beta,\sqrt{\frac{eD J^3M^2\beta^3}{3\eta}}\right\}.
\]

The rounding to an integer is understood. For fixed parameters this is constant in volume.

### Sufficient first-order fallback

The even-coefficient refinement is not needed for the bridge. Bounding the full conjugation difference by `J(exp(JMt)-1)` instead gives directly

\[
\|\log P(\delta)+\delta H\|
\le {2m\over M}(e^{JM\delta}-1-JM\delta),
\]

and normalized log-partition error at most

\[
{2Dr\over M}(e^x-1-x)
\le D J^2M e^x\frac{\beta^2}{r}.
\]

Thus even the simpler first-order argument already supplies a constant-in-volume step count.

## Proof

### 1. Finite active cones under disjoint-layer conjugation

Take a local operator `a` supported on at most `k` sites. Conjugation by one disjoint layer only involves gates whose supports intersect the current support. At most the current support size many gates are active. Their union with the current support has size at most `k` times that support size.

Therefore conjugation by any ordered subsequence of at most `q` layers can be written, on this particular operator, as a product of at most `M = k + ... + k^q` active local conjugations. The active cone depends only on supports, not on `t`, and works identically for `t` and `-t`.

Each such conjugation is the superoperator

\[
e^{-t\,\operatorname{ad}_{h_b}/2},\qquad
\|\operatorname{ad}_{h_b}/2\|_{\mathrm{op}\to\mathrm{op}}\le J.
\]

Let `U(t)` be any such ordered layer product, and let `F(t)=U(t)aU(t)^{-1}`. Expanding this *finite product* of entire superoperator exponentials gives, coefficient by coefficient,

\[
\|[t^p]F(t)\|\le\|a\|\frac{(JM)^p}{p!}. \tag{3}
\]

This is an absolutely convergent series bound, not a truncated BCH argument. It follows by summing the multinomial coefficients for the finite product of exponential series.

When `a` is Hermitian, each layer factor is Hermitian for real `t`, so

\[
U(-t)=U(t)^{-\dagger},\qquad F(t)^\dagger=F(-t).
\]

Hence the Hermitian part of `F` consists only of its even Taylor coefficients. Since `F(0)=a`, (3) implies

\[
\|\operatorname{Herm}F(t)-a\|
\le\|a\|[\cosh(JMt)-1]. \tag{4}
\]

### 2. A relative evolution with no full-Hamiltonian imaginary conjugation

Set

\[
R(t)=Q(t)e^{tH/2},\qquad G(t)=R'(t)R(t)^{-1}.
\]

Product differentiation gives

\[
G(t)=Q'(t)Q(t)^{-1}+\tfrac12Q(t)HQ(t)^{-1}
=\tfrac12\sum_{j=1}^q\left[
\operatorname{Ad}_{Q(t)}H_j-
\operatorname{Ad}_{U_{>j}(t)}H_j\right], \tag{5}
\]

where `U_{>j}=E_q ... E_{j+1}` (empty product is the identity).

The crucial point is that (5) contains only finite-depth layer conjugations. It contains no `e^{tH} a e^{-tH}`. Thus extensive operator norms do not appear inside an exponential bound.

Expand every `H_j` into its local terms, subtract and add each original `h_a`, and use (4). Since there are `m` terms and the prefactor is `1/2`,

\[
\|\operatorname{Herm}G(t)\|
\le mJ[\cosh(JMt)-1]=:g(t). \tag{6}
\]

### 3. Singular-value comparison, then the operator logarithm

For every vector `v`, `R'=GR` implies

\[
\frac{d}{dt}\|R(t)v\|^2
=2\langle R(t)v,\operatorname{Herm}G(t)R(t)v\rangle.
\]

By the scalar differential inequalities from (6), with `R(0)=I`,

\[
e^{-2a(\delta)}I\preceq R(\delta)^\dagger R(\delta)
\preceq e^{2a(\delta)}I,
\quad
a(\delta)=\int_0^\delta g(t)dt
={m\over M}[\sinh(JM\delta)-JM\delta]. \tag{7}
\]

Since `R^dagger R = e^{delta H/2} P(delta) e^{delta H/2}`, congruence gives

\[
e^{-2a(\delta)}e^{-\delta H}
\preceq P(\delta)
\preceq e^{2a(\delta)}e^{-\delta H}. \tag{8}
\]

The matrix logarithm is operator monotone on positive definite matrices. Applying it to (8) yields

\[
-\delta H-2a(\delta)I
\preceq\log P(\delta)
\preceq-\delta H+2a(\delta)I,
\]

which is (1).

**Important:** powers of (8) are not taken in Loewner order; that would be invalid. The logarithm is taken first.

### 4. From the effective generator to the partition function

For Hermitian `A,B`,

\[
|\log\operatorname{Tr}e^A-\log\operatorname{Tr}e^B|\le\|A-B\|.
\]

For completeness, interpolate `B+s(A-B)`; the derivative of its log-trace-exponential is the expectation of `A-B` in a positive normalized Gibbs state, so its absolute value is at most `||A-B||`.

Apply this with `A=r log P(beta/r)` and `B=-beta H`. Equation (1) and `m<=nD` give the first inequality in (2). For `x>=0`, Taylor's integral remainder gives `sinh(x)-x <= x^3 e^x/6`, proving the second.

## Free energy and ground-energy density

Let `f_beta=-(beta n)^{-1} log Tr e^{-beta H}` and let `e_0=E_0(H)/n`. If each local spin dimension is at most `d`,

\[
e_0-\frac{\log d}{\beta}\le f_\beta\le e_0.
\]

The product formula estimates `f_beta` with error at most the right side of (2) divided by `beta`. Thus taking `beta >= 2 log(d)/epsilon` and choosing `r` to make that free-energy-density error at most `epsilon/2` gives an `epsilon`-additive ground-energy-density estimate, provided the approximate product partition function can itself be evaluated to sufficient log-density accuracy.

No claim is made here that arbitrary signed local tensor weights can already be compiled into fixed-width exact #SAT with acceptable precision/size. That is a separate obligation.

## Why low-temperature ordering does not obstruct this bound

The argument compares the logarithm of a *single positive step* to `-delta H`, then takes powers in the logarithm. It never transports local errors for imaginary time `beta`, and never requires locality of the exact effective Hamiltonian `-(1/delta) log P`. Low-temperature Gibbs correlations and expander geometry therefore do not enter. Constants can be very large in `k,D`, but are independent of `n`.

# Independent audit: volume-uniform symmetric imaginary-time product formula

Date: 2026-10-29 UTC. Auditor: `test_thermal_counting_bridge/audit_uniform_trotter`.

## Verdict

**PASS.** The proposed elementary argument establishes a volume-uniform
second-order log-partition-density approximation for arbitrary bounded-degree,
bounded-strength, finite-spin, (k)-local Hamiltonians. It needs neither a
stoquasticity assumption nor a geometric decomposition nor a high-temperature
restriction on the target inverse temperature. The number of time slices can
depend on inverse temperature and target density error, but not on volume.

This receipt audits the physics approximation only. It makes **no assessment of
the counting-complexity reduction**, arithmetic precision, weight compilation,
or the supplied exact-counting algorithm. It makes **no novelty claim** and does
not claim the argument is a new theorem in the literature.

## Assumptions and definitions

Let (H=\sum_{a=1}^{m}h_a) on (n) sites. Each (h_a) is Hermitian,
has nonempty support of size at most (k\ge1), and has spectral norm at most
(J\ge0). Every site belongs to at most (D\ge1) term supports. Thus
(m\le Dn). Empty-support scalar terms can be removed and handled exactly.
The cases (m=0) or (J=0) are exact and need no bound.

The term-overlap graph has maximum degree at most (k(D-1)). A proper coloring
uses (q\le k(D-1)+1) colors. Write (H=\sum_{j=1}^{q}H_j), with each
(H_j) a sum of pairwise disjoint-support terms. Set

\[
 E_j(t)=e^{-tH_j/2},\quad Q(t)=E_q(t)\cdots E_1(t),\quad
 P(t)=Q(t)^\dagger Q(t),\quad M=\sum_{\ell=1}^{q}k^\ell.
\]

For β≥0, integer (r\ge1), δ=β/r, and (x=JM\delta), the accepted
bound is

\[
\boxed{
 \frac1n\left|\log\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H}
 -\log\operatorname{Tr}P(\beta/r)^r\right|
 \le \frac{2Dr}{M}(\sinh x-x)
 \le \frac{DJ^3M^2e^x\beta^3}{3r^2}.
}
\]

In particular, taking (r\ge JM\beta) replaces (e^x) by (e).
For any fixed β and density error ε>0, an integer

\[
 r\ge\max\left\{JM\beta,
 \sqrt{eDJ^3M^2\beta^3/(3\epsilon)}\right\}
\]

is sufficient. This bound is loose in its local constants but independent of n.
For free-energy density, divide the log-partition-density error by β when
β>0.

## Checks of the decisive steps

### 1. Local conjugation has a volume-independent power-series majorant

Consider (F(t)=U(t)h_aU(t)^{-1}), where (U) is a prefix/suffix product
of at most (q) colored layer exponentials in the order relevant below.
During one layer, only gates whose supports intersect the current support cone
need be retained. Since the gates in a layer are disjoint, at most (s) gates
are active on a cone of size (s); the next cone has size at most (ks).
Starting from size at most (k), at most

\[
k+k^2+\cdots+k^q=M
\]

local gates are retained. All removed gates commute with the operator at the
point at which they are removed. The cone is an upper bound fixed from supports,
so the same removal is valid at every real or complex t and for both signs of t.

Each retained conjugation is

\[
 e^{-t\operatorname{ad}_{h_b}/2},\qquad
 \|\operatorname{ad}_{h_b}/2\|\le\|h_b\|\le J,
\]

as a linear map in the spectral operator norm. Multiplying its absolutely
convergent power series shows

\[
\|[t^p]F(t)\|\le J\frac{(JM)^p}{p!}.
\]

This coefficient estimate does not use an extensive norm ‖H‖.

Every factor in (U(t)) is a Hermitian exponential, and the ordered product
satisfies (U(-t)=U(t)^{-\dagger}). Therefore, for real t,

\[
 F(t)^\dagger=F(-t),\qquad
 \operatorname{Herm}F(t)=\tfrac12(F(t)+F(-t)).
\]

Odd Taylor coefficients are anti-Hermitian; even coefficients are Hermitian.
Consequently

\[
\|\operatorname{Herm}F(t)-h_a\|
\le J\big(\cosh(JMt)-1\big),\qquad t\ge0.
\]

### 2. Relative propagator cancels full-H imaginary-time evolution

Define (R(t)=Q(t)e^{tH/2}). Exact differentiation gives

\[
 R'(t)=G(t)R(t),\qquad
 G(t)=Q'(t)Q(t)^{-1}+\tfrac12Q(t)HQ(t)^{-1}.
\]

Let (U_{>j}(t)=E_q(t)\cdots E_{j+1}(t)), with the empty product equal
to I. Since (E_j' E_j^{-1}=-H_j/2),

\[
 G(t)=\frac12\sum_{j=1}^q\sum_{a\in j}
 \left(\operatorname{Ad}_{Q(t)}h_a
       -\operatorname{Ad}_{U_{>j}(t)}h_a\right).
\]

The local (h_a) terms cancel when Hermitian parts are taken and the bound from
step 1 is applied. Hence

\[
 \|\operatorname{Herm}G(t)\|
 \le mJ\big(\cosh(JMt)-1\big).
\]

This is the key point: no full-H imaginary-time conjugation is estimated. All
conjugations to be bounded have constant layer depth.

### 3. Two-sided relative Loewner bound, not an additive global norm bound

For each vector v, exact differentiation gives

\[
 \frac{d}{dt}\|R(t)v\|^2
 =2\langle R(t)v,\operatorname{Herm}G(t)R(t)v\rangle.
\]

Scalar Grönwall in both directions, using R(0)=I, yields

\[
 e^{-2b}I\preceq R(\delta)^\dagger R(\delta)\preceq e^{2b}I,
 \qquad b=\frac mM(\sinh x-x).
\]

Since (R^\dagger R=e^{\delta H/2}P(\delta)e^{\delta H/2}), congruence by
(e^{-\delta H/2}) gives

\[
e^{-2b}e^{-\delta H}\preceq P(\delta)
\preceq e^{2b}e^{-\delta H}.
\]

### 4. Operator-monotone logarithm avoids an invalid power step

Logarithm is operator monotone on positive definite matrices. Applying it to
the preceding sandwich is valid, and scalar prefactors commute with everything:

\[
-2bI-\delta H\preceq\log P(\delta)
\preceq2bI-\delta H.
\]

Thus ‖log P(δ)+δH‖≤2b. The proof does **not** claim that raising the
Loewner sandwich to the r-th power preserves Loewner order; that generally
invalid inference is unnecessary.

### 5. Log partition is spectral-norm Lipschitz

For Hermitian A,B, the min-max principle gives

\[
 |\log\operatorname{Tr}e^A-\log\operatorname{Tr}e^B|
 \le\|A-B\|.
\]

This follows by comparing their ordered eigenvalues; it does not require the
matrix exponential to be operator monotone. Apply it with
(A=r\log P(\beta/r)) and (B=-\beta H), then use m≤Dn. Finally,
(\sinh x-x\le x^3e^x/6) for x≥0 gives the displayed simplified bound.

## Lower-order fallback also passed

Discarding Hermitian-part cancellation gives

\[
\|G(t)\|\le mJ(e^{JMt}-1)
\]

and the weaker but sufficient guarantee

\[
\frac1n|\log Z-\log Z_r|
\le\frac{2Dr}{M}(e^x-1-x)
\le DJ^2M e^x\frac{\beta^2}{r}.
\]

Both arguments have been checked algebraically. Numerical examples can be
helpful regression tests but are not needed for this proof and cannot establish
the volume-uniform result by themselves.

## Scope boundaries

- Local dimension may be any finite value for the analytic bound; an algorithmic
  statement additionally needs a fixed/local representation bound.
- Local strengths J must be bounded independently of volume for constant r.
- Degree means term-support incidence, not an unstated graph-degree surrogate.
- Positivity of P comes from (Q^\dagger Q); individual matrix entries may have
  signs or complex phases.
- No thermodynamic-limit existence or differentiability is assumed.
- A global O(n) log-partition error is appropriate for density approximation;
  it is not a constant multiplicative approximation of the partition function.
- This receipt does not settle whether constant-precision local weights are
  sufficient for the proposed signed-counting reduction.

# Canonical raw divergence can acquire an unknown nonlinear projective chart

## Result and acceptance contract

Input: a rational polynomial vector field `f` on `n` original coordinates, with no chart, inverse, projective matrix, or observable dictionary supplied. Manufacture

    q=-div(f)/(n+1),       T=D+q,       D=f dot grad.

Acquire the cyclic polynomial space

    V=span{1,T1,T^2 1,...}

by exact sparse elimination or circuit-jet evaluation plus the identity-admission rules in `PROOF.md`. If it closes at dimension `n+1`, choose the acquired basis as

    phi=(1,psi_1,...,psi_n)^T,       T phi=A phi.

Next **construct** a polynomial inverse `H` of `psi` by formal series iteration, and admit it only after checking both global identities

    H(psi(x))=x,       psi(H(y))=y.

No inference from constant nonzero Jacobian to global invertibility is used. A singular basepoint, failed identities, nontermination within a degree budget, deficient cyclic rank, or excessive cyclic rank returns an explicit not-acquired result.

For every admitted raw input the exact original flow is

    z(t)=exp(tA) (1,psi(x0)),
    x(t)=H(z_1(t)/z_0(t),...,z_n(t)/z_0(t)).

This holds on the connected nonsingular interval containing zero. The expression is exact; stable numerical evaluation has separate precision/conditioning costs. Input randomization does not turn finite-point checking into deterministic certification: the current experiment has exact coefficient replay of closure and both inverse identities.

The output now has a minimal possible `n+1` projective linear coordinate count, but **the inverse polynomial still has real degree/circuit/bit cost**. It has not vanished into a supplied decoder.

## Why this acquires hidden information

Suppose, as a sufficient completeness class rather than an admission premise, that the raw system is `f=h_*g`, where `h` is an unknown polynomial automorphism and

    g(y)=a+B y-(c^T y)y.

Define the homogeneous matrix

    M = [[0,c^T],[a,B]],       kappa=tr(M)/(n+1).

As proved in `PROOF.md`, constant Jacobian determinant of `h` implies divergence covariance. The raw operator `T` is transported to the action of `M-kappa I` on the hidden affine-linear functions `1,y_1,...,y_n`.

Assume the homogeneous denominator row `e_0^T` is cyclic for `M`: the rows

    e_0^T, e_0^T M, ..., e_0^T M^n

are independent. This is an open, nonempty algebraic condition on `M`; it is a genuine boundary, not a universal property. The acquired cyclic space then has dimension exactly `n+1` and equals the pullback of all hidden affine-linear functions. Thus the acquired `psi` is an invertible affine transformation of `h^{-1}`, and it has a polynomial inverse of degree `deg(h)`.

The algorithm does not receive cyclicity or `h`. It observes the actual rank, checks closure, builds the inverse, and tests the two identities. The hidden-class argument proves that these operations will eventually succeed at sufficiently large budgets. Genericity is used only to specify that completeness class. For example, affine-linear fields have constant divergence and their `T`-orbit of `1` is one-dimensional; this particular chart route correctly fails despite their being easy to solve by other means.

For an accepted inverse, the transformed field is visibly projective:

    psi'=A_tail,0+A_tail,tail psi - (A_00+A_0,tail psi) psi.

Since a polynomial inverse forces constant Jacobian determinant, divergence covariance further gives `tr(A)=0`. These are consequences/checks, not inputs supplying the chart.

## Constructive inverse, with no Jacobian-conjecture shortcut

Let `c=psi(0)` and `J=Dpsi(0)`. If `J` is invertible, set

    F(x)=J^{-1}(psi(x)-c)=x+N(x),       ord N>=2.

The formal inverse is the fixed point `G(z)=z-N(G(z))`. Starting from `G=z`, each iteration determines one more homogeneous degree. At a tested degree budget `E`, perform `E-1` iterations, truncating every polynomial to total degree `E`. Then test both exact polynomial identities `F(G(z))=z` and `G(F(x))=x`. If they hold, return

    H(y)=G(J^{-1}(y-c)).

If a polynomial inverse of degree `e` exists, a budget `E>=e` obtains it. Budgets `1,2,4,8,...` have total cost bounded polynomially by the first successful degree (or by the explicit final budget). Without a successful global identity test, the formal inverse remains merely local/formal and the algorithm returns no global chart.

For circuit input this can avoid multivariate monomial expansion. Insert a scalar homogenizing parameter `t`, keep coefficients of `G(tz)` through `t^E`, and carry each coefficient as an arithmetic circuit in `z`. Evaluate the circuit for `F` over the truncated ring. Ordinary convolution uses `O(E^2)` arithmetic-circuit operations per source gate per iteration; `O(E)` iterations give polynomial circuit size and arithmetic work in `E`, `n`, and source size. Shared DAGs must actually be retained. The current implementation uses exact expanded polynomials for this inverse step; the circuit construction is a proof-level route, not a claim that the existing script already avoids expansion here.

The global circuit identities require either randomized PIT with independent fresh randomness and degree bounds, or exact coefficient verification with its cost paid. Intermediate rational heights and the degree of the inverse are retained. A small forward circuit alone does not guarantee a cheap inverse. No unrestricted inversion algorithm or solution of the Jacobian conjecture is claimed.

## A proved exponential representation separation

This is a separation from **original-state-containing density-module linearization** and dense polynomial dictionaries, not a lower bound against every conventional symbolic/projective algorithm.

For integers `n>=2` and `e>=2`, let `b=e+1`, set

    lambda_j=b^(j-1), j=1,...,n,
    M=[[0,1,...,1],[0,lambda_1,0,...],...,[0,...,lambda_n]],
    g_j(y)=lambda_j y_j - y_j sum_k y_k.

Let the hidden polynomial automorphism be the triangular shear

    h_j(y)=y_j (j<n),
    h_n(y)=y_n+(sum_{j<n} y_j)^e.

This specifies a family used to prove a resource claim, not a supplied chart to the compiler. The raw pushed-forward field has a division-free arithmetic circuit of size polynomial in `n` and `log e`, degree at most `2e`, and rational input coefficient bit lengths polynomial in `n log(e+1)`. Substitution uses the compact inverse shear; generating the family does not place that inverse in the acquisition input.

**Small-chart route.** The eigenvalues of `M` are distinct. Eigenlinear forms of the homogeneous flow can be chosen as

    ell_0=Z_0-sum_j Z_j/lambda_j,       ell_j=Z_j.

Thus `Z_0=ell_0+sum_j ell_j/lambda_j` has a nonzero component on every eigenspace. Its cyclic rank is `n+1`; the chart route acquires an `n+1`-dimensional module. The chart inverse has degree `e`, and the circuit formal-inverse construction above has polynomial arithmetic cost in `n,e` and the acquired circuit size, not in `binomial(n+e,e)`.

**Original-state density route.** At weight `m`, its module must contain `1,h_1,...,h_n` in hidden coordinates. If `m<e`, the highest-degree part of repeated `T_m h_n` is multiplied at each step by a nonzero scalar times `sum y_j`, so degrees increase strictly forever. There is no finite original-state-containing module at those weights.

At `m=e`, the seed `1` corresponds under homogenization to `Z_0^e`. Its expansion in the eigenforms has a nonzero coefficient for every monomial

    ell_0^alpha_0 ... ell_n^alpha_n,       sum alpha_j=e.

The eigenvalues of these monomials, before an irrelevant common trace shift, are `sum_{j>=1} alpha_j b^(j-1)`. All are distinct: these are base-`b` expansions with digits in `0,...,e=b-1`. There are exactly `binomial(n+e,e)` of them. The Vandermonde criterion therefore gives a cyclic dimension of exactly that size already from seed `1`.

For `m>e`, the eigenvalue-support set from `Z_0^m` contains the set for `Z_0^e` (increase only `alpha_0`); all expansion coefficients are positive, so colliding eigenvalues do not cancel. Thus every finite original-state-containing integer-weight density lift has dimension at least `binomial(n+e,e)`, with equality achieved at weight `e`.

Taking `e=n`, the old linear-module dimension is `binomial(2n,n)` while the acquired chart uses `n+1` linear coordinates plus a degree-`n` inverse circuit. This is an exponential dimension separation on compact raw circuits. It is not merely another small hidden-shear benchmark. The nonlinear decoder is the mathematical reason the original-state linear lift need not carry the entire symmetric-power representation.

An equally informed conventional algorithm can exploit the same acquired chart and inverse. No exponential lower bound against arbitrary Lie/projective/Darboux recognition algorithms follows from the representation separation.

## Implemented result

`acquired_projective_chart.py` takes the raw coefficients only. On the recorded test it acquires

    phi=(1, x^4-2x^2 y+x^2-x+y^2-y, x^2-y),

with generator

    A=[[-8/3,-1,0], [0,-5/3,6], [0,0,13/3]].

The degree-one and degree-two formal inverses fail global checks; degree four passes both. The returned inverse is stored explicitly in `chart_results.json`. Twelve independent trajectory checks agree within `1.7e-16`; polynomial closure and both inverse identities are exact. This is a full acquired three-dimensional projective representation and original-coordinate decoder, not only a latent predictor.

## Conventional ancestry and nonclaims

The projectivization of linear systems, Riccati/Lie--Scheffers theory, density Lie derivatives, Darboux polynomial cofactors, and formal polynomial inversion are established mathematics. The sources and strongest symbolic first-integral comparator are in `PROOF.md`. Projective Riccati systems were explicitly linearized long before this work: *Linearization of homogeneous Riccati equations* (1983), https://doi.org/10.1016/0375-9601(83)90647-3 ; see also Carinena--de Lucas, *Lie systems: theory, generalisations, and applications*, https://www.impan.pl/shop/publication/transaction/download/product/88196 . These are not evidence that an unknown polynomial chart has been acquired from raw equations, but they prohibit claiming projective linearization itself as new.

The current contribution is an independently checkable **raw acquisition composition**: canonical divergence, a low-rank cyclic density module, actual inverse manufacture, and original-state reconstruction. Historical priority of that complete combination remains unestablished. No general claim about chaos, arbitrary polynomial flows, data-only identification, noisy robustness, numerical stability, or scientific usefulness follows automatically.

The substantive review is `latent_integrable_geometry/audit/relative_interface_20261029/POLYNOMIAL_BIT_VERDICT.md`; it accepts the repaired mathematical construction, not all software or a priority claim. No superiority over equally informed inverse-spectral methods is claimed.

## Proposed theorem

Input consists of N>=3, explicit rational a_i>0 and b_i, rational time T, and integer p>=1. Let B be the total binary input length excluding T and p. There is a deterministic algorithm returning rational approximations to every a_i(T),b_i(T) with absolute error <=2^-p in bit time polynomial in N,B,bitlength(T),p.

No spectral-gap, simple-spectrum, nonexceptional-divisor, prescribed-pivot, or lower-norming-weight promise is supplied. Small positive input a_i are charged by their actual rational bit length. The statement is for mathematical Toda instances, not physical data acquisition or approximate integrability. It is not currently a complete certified software claim.

## Exact preprocessing and representations

Compute C=product a_i and the transfer polynomial p_Toda=C tr M by polynomial-time rational arithmetic. Avoid the symbol p for this polynomial in implementation, since p is also output precision. Set F=p_Toda²−4C². Positive periodic Jacobi theory bounds branch multiplicity by two. Exact rational gcd gives K=gcd(F,F'), then reduced squarefree curve F_red=F/K². Its genus g=N−1−deg K. All polynomial coefficient heights are polynomial in N,B; polynomial gcd/division is performed over Q, not a splitting field.

The branch roots of the radical F/K include the closed nodes and have a nonzero integer discriminant after denominators are cleared. The elementary discriminant bound supplies log(1/Delta)=poly(N,B). Root magnitudes satisfy an explicit M=poly(H+1), so log M=poly(N,B). For g=0, return the unique physical isospectral point, namely the initial data.

The principal Dirichlet polynomial G of the initial (N−1)-site Jacobi matrix is computed exactly over Q. Divide G by K to retain the active divisor. Each active mu is represented by a rational isolating interval and its polynomial, with refinable rational approximations. The sheet is obtained from kappa=M11(mu) and y=2C kappa−p_Toda(mu), then y_red=y/K(mu). The denominator is nonzero at active nodes and has a derived separation/height bound. Endpoint coincidences are detected by gcd(G/K,F_red), not by waiting for floating intervals to disjoin. Closed divisor nodes are stored through K and kappa=±1, whose sign is separated by gcd(K,p_Toda∓2C).

No exact primitive element for the compositum of all branch or divisor roots is constructed. All later analytic calculations use independently refinable certified rational enclosures. This prevents a hidden exponential algebraic-field degree from entering the bit claim.

## Initialize, double, reconstruct

1. Obtain the initial physical signed-angle coordinates to the required accuracy on the fixed reduced curve. At endpoints the signed local coordinate is used; evaluating square roots may double requested precision but does not change polynomial complexity.
2. Use `LOCAL_FLOW_INITIALIZATION.md`, with its two audit corrections, to find a small-time divisor on this SAME exact curve. The exact reduced velocity is (0,...,0,-2). Choose m so tau=T/2^m lies inside the derived inverse collar; m=poly(N,B)+O(bitlength(T)).
3. Perform m relative operations E~2D−D0 using the normalized rational rounded-kernel, separated-point and same-sheet root construction. The interface audit must charge the OUTER selected-zero radius, not merely the inner existence radius. At each call, output a fresh fixed-precision signed-angle representation of a genuine physical divisor. No inherited algebraic height is propagated into the next call.
4. Reattach fixed closed nodes and use the full inverse-spectral decoder, including norming weights and finite-Jacobi reconstruction. Use separation of F/K, not merely of F_red, in bounds involving the full divisor. The established positive lower bounds on a_i and norming weights provide polynomial-log physical-output conditioning.

The mathematical group-law argument is classical; it does not require a period matrix. Every short local displacement defines a direct Abel-error lift. Relative doubling doubles the prior lift and adds the current local lift. Nonspeciality gives a unique effective degree-g representative and the explicit inverse collar converts direct error to physical coordinates even if an algebraic section had exceptional intermediate zeros.

## Bit accounting of one relative operation

Let q denote the chosen matrix rounding precision. Each section matrix entry has magnitude <=2^U where U=poly(N,B); the rounded integer matrix therefore has entry height O(q+U). A nonzero exact rational kernel vector can be produced by fraction-free elimination. Minor bounds give normalized coefficient height O(g(q+U+log g)). No lower bound on a numerical singular value is used.

The rational norm polynomial A²−F_red B² has degree at most4g and coefficient height polynomial in g,q,B. Exact gcd(A,B), squarefree factorization, zero multiplicities and the two infinity orders are therefore polynomial-bit operations. The appropriate primary root-isolation import is Mehlhorn–Sagraloff–Wang, *From approximate factorization to root isolation* (ISSAC2013 / JSC2015, DOI10.1016/j.jsc.2014.02.001): rational integer coefficient inputs admit polynomial-bit isolation/refinement of all complex roots with multiplicities. The distinct-root count is available from exact gcd, not an oracle. Their near-optimal bound is not needed; a polynomial bound suffices.

For the reduced coprime pair A0,B0, B0 is nonzero at every root of A0²−F_red B0². A nonzero integer resultant, coefficient heights and root bounds give log(1/|B0(mu)|)=poly(g,q,B), charging the sheet quotient. Common factors and ramification points are treated separately, so this assertion is never applied at a true common root.

The norm/same-sheet lemma demands q polynomial in g,B,log(1/delta); matching and projection have derived polynomial-log margins. Thus each call costs polynomial(N,B,m,p). Fresh rounding to the chosen angle representation prevents algebraic coefficient heights from multiplying across m calls.

## Error budget and outstanding review questions

Let kappa_dec be the derived physical output Lipschitz bound on the physical collar. Set delta<=2^(-m-3) min(eta_col,2^-p/kappa_dec), where eta_col is the uniform inverse-collar radius in direct Abel coordinates. Ensure initialization direct error<=delta, each relative operation adds<=delta, and final decoding error<=2^(-p-1). Then e_m<2^(m+1)delta<=min(eta_col,2^-p/kappa_dec)/4. Thus all uses of the inverse collar are valid even for coarse requested accuracy, and total physical error<=2^-p.

The independent review explicitly checked compatibility of the chart/outer-selection error budget, closed-gap extraction, physical decoder conditioning, and the root-isolation import. Its exact source is MSW arXiv:1301.4870v2 Theorem5, read in full. Remaining archival consolidation and fully certified implementation are distinct from the mathematical polynomial-complexity conclusion. The review is substantive internal review, not exhaustive external peer review of the entire classical Toda literature.

At the repaired reviewed scope, this is a uniform bit-complexity result for full-state exact-input Toda prediction, including degenerate closed gaps. It does not establish a new physical principle, a general integrability-discovery theorem, robustness under unknown perturbations, or historical novelty. The raw hidden-Toda recognition calculation is separate and has a strong linear self-adjoint polar-kernel comparator. Known inverse-scattering methods already compute long-time Toda solutions without time stepping in other settings. Any broader significance must come from a genuinely new transfer or capability, not relabeling this classical composition.

The first assembly incorrectly wrote M22 for the initial Floquet multiplier. With T_N...T_1 acting on (psi_1,psi_0)=(1,0), the Dirichlet condition gives psi_N=0 and kappa=psi_(N+1)=M11(mu). M22 is its reciprocal and selects the conjugate sheet. The executed N=3 regression detects a different isospectral physical state if M22 is used. The theorem candidate above is corrected; the rejected regression is preserved by the physical-bridge implementation.

From its complex zeta near the unit circle, normalize to modulus one, choose a cardinal rotation with real part at least1/2 using a comparison with slack, and form t=Im(u)/(1+Re(u)). Round t to a fixed-precision dyadic and return the exact circle point ((1-t²)+2it)/(1+t²), rotated back. The parametrization has derivative norm<=2. The two original gap endpoints plus this rational circle point define mu and y on the fixed curve using one square root, with polynomial descriptive degree and height. The fixed D0 remains its ORIGINAL exact algebraic description; errors in interval evaluation of D0 count against each call's delta. Thus neither initial reference drift nor exponentially growing composita are hidden in the theorem.

## Decision

**At the mathematical existence level, yes:** for explicitly supplied rational positive periodic Toda initial data and rational target time, the repaired lemmas supply a polynomial-bit algorithm with original-state max error epsilon, including exact closed gaps. I do not identify a remaining difficult mathematical oracle to assume. A full executable is not a prerequisite to that theorem.

This conclusion uses the explicit perturbation/outer-matching repair in `INDEPENDENT_INTERFACE_AUDIT.md`, the inexact-domain/forward-error repairs in `LOCAL_INITIALIZATION_REVIEW.md`, the established Toda Lax/inverse-spectral facts already acknowledged in the governing draft, and the precise univariate root-isolation primitive below. The earlier draft *without* these repairs is not the complete proof. This is not a general raw-equation compiler, no practical efficient exponent is claimed, and an equally informed classical algorithm can use the same method.

## Precise root-isolation import, checked

Mehlhorn–Sagraloff–Wang, *From Approximate Factorization to Root Isolation with Application to Cylindrical Algebraic Decomposition*, [arXiv:1301.4870v2, Theorem 5](https://arxiv.org/html/1301.4870), states that an integer polynomial of degree n and coefficient bits tau has all distinct roots and their multiplicities isolated in soft-O(n^3+n^2 tau) bit operations; refinement to disk radius below 2^-kappa costs soft-O(n^3+n^2 tau+n kappa). Its proof computes the distinct-root count from p/gcd(p,p'), and normalizes by the exact leading coefficient. Thus there is no distinct-root-count or leading-coefficient promise in our rational-polynomial application. Clear denominators first. I inspected the theorem and proof, not just its abstract. The first supplied PDF URL failed with a 502; the accessible arXiv full text established the needed contract.

## Finite-size representation and bit ledger

Let B be total binary size of initial rational a,b, let L_T be rational time bit size, and let b=max(0,ceil(log2(1/epsilon))).

1. **Fixed spectral data.** Transfer recurrence, rational polynomial gcds, exact division, and squarefree root isolation compute p,F,K,Ftilde and the radical. Their degrees are O(N), heights polynomial(N,B). The initial Dirichlet roots are roots of an O(N)-degree rational polynomial. Their sheets are evaluated using the original transfer recurrence, and reduced sheets divide by K(mu), not |K(mu)|. Active roots are separated from closed nodes by the radical-derived separation. Exact closed-node multipliers are found by gcd with p-2C and p+2C. All of this is polynomial-bit, with no perturbation of closed gaps.

2. **Computable uniform constants.** Let S be an integer majorizing the logarithms of every explicit forward/inverse, chart, collar, coefficient, and physical decoder bound used in the proof, plus their reciprocals where appropriate. The displayed product/discriminant/Gram formulas make S polynomial(N,B). These are rationally overestimated bounds, not measured condition-number oracles. In particular the very small radical separation and a_* have polynomial logarithms.

3. **Fixed working accuracy.** Choose m=O(L_T+S) so tau=T/2^m is inside the initialization collar. Set a direct budget delta <=2^(-m-cS-b-c), for a sufficiently large absolute c after combining the displayed Lipschitz factors; cap the final accumulated error by a fraction of the collar radius as well as epsilon/kappa_dec. All needed angle/ambient/Abel tolerances then have negative logarithm O(m+b+poly(N,B)). Initialization is evaluated by scaled Taylor series and the repaired inexact contraction at this precision.

4. **Each arithmetic call.** The separation h, ambient matching radius d0, and chart existence radius rho all have negative logarithm polynomial(N,B,m,b). The residual theorem requires q=O(N(log(1/rho)+S))+O(log N) bits. The rounded evaluation matrix has O(N^2) rational entries of size O(q+S). Integer minor/Hadamard bounds give a kernel vector with numerator/denominator bits O(N(q+S+log N)), even if the exact rounded matrix has deficient rank. Normalizing by its largest coefficient preserves polynomial size. No pivot size is needed.

5. **Section bookkeeping.** Clearing denominators in A^2-Ftilde B^2 gives an integer polynomial of degree O(N), coefficient height polynomial(N,q,S). Exact gcds and squarefree decomposition are polynomial in those quantities. The imported theorem isolates/refines all its roots in polynomial work. Sheet quotients have denominator inverse <=2^poly(N,height) by the exact nonzero resultant after gcd removal. Common factors are handled separately, including branch multiplicity; infinity orders use only O(N) rational Taylor coefficients. Therefore the extra precision to produce ambient root balls is polynomial. The outer-radius inequality in the interface note charges *every selected occurrence*, not merely the guaranteed closest zero.

6. **Reset representations after every call.** Do not carry a product of all algebraic root fields, and do not retain the exact algebraic residual coordinates through repeated calls. After the collar and gap identification, compute zeta and its unit normalization. Rotate by a cardinal unit so its real part is at least 1/2 (certified approximate comparison with slack suffices), write t=Im(u)/(1+Re(u)), approximate t by a b_work-bit dyadic, and store the exact rational circle point ((1-t^2)+2it)/(1+t^2), rotated back. The derivative of this parametrization has modulus <=2. The corresponding physical point uses the original exact two gap endpoints and one square root. It is on the unchanged curve exactly and has polynomial-bit descriptive size. Each point's algebraic degree is O(N^2), not an exponentially large joint field. Independent interval evaluation suffices for the next rounded matrix. Precision depends on requested accuracy, not on previous exact section heights.

7. **Physical decoding.** Include the fixed closed nodes in the full finite Dirichlet polynomial. Evaluate stable reciprocal Floquet branches, the positive weight formula, and the moment Gram matrix. Its smallest eigenvalue has inverse <=2^poly(N,B), as proved from a_* and separated nodes. Cholesky/orthogonalization can use rational interval arithmetic: every leading Schur complement has smallest eigenvalue at least the full matrix lower bound, so all square roots/divisions have derived denominator margins. Moment magnitudes are <=2^poly(N,B); differentiating the O(poly N) arithmetic steps gives <=2^poly(N,B) error amplification. Set working precision to absorb that factor, and round a,b to epsilon/2. This charges the decoder algorithm, not merely its formal condition number.

8. **Composition.** Every call costs poly(N,B,m,b), and there are m calls. The direct torus error satisfies e_next<=2e+delta because every stored divisor is a true physical point of the same fixed curve. The fixed reference D0 may be evaluated to arbitrary interval precision from its original algebraic description; approximation errors in each evaluation must be included in delta, not treated as changing the reference silently. Since m=poly(N,B,L_T), total work is polynomial(N,B,L_T,b). All final error comparisons are made within the collar before applying the physical decoder bound.

## Residual obligations, classified honestly

**Not unresolved mathematical capabilities:** exact closed-gap detection; small initial step on the fixed curve; near-conjugate or edge divisor arithmetic without pivot promises; polynomial-height root/sheet/infinity bookkeeping; direct-error composition; original-state decoding. The above lemmas and primitive contracts address them at polynomial-complexity granularity.

**Still needed for an archival full proof:** consolidate constants and notation, explicitly state the classical spectral/Abel algebraic-geometric imports, insert the two local guards and the outer-selection budget into the main theorem, and spell out the input/output encoding and fixed-reference invariant. These are proof-writing/verification obligations; the present independent review is not equivalent to exhaustive peer review of every preceding imported Toda derivation.

**Engineering gaps:** certified arbitrary-genus interval implementation, actual precision admission tests, closed-gap and repeated-doubling end-to-end regressions, and practical operation counts. The existing genus-one numerical phase matches do not certify these. A low-precision case can have excellent apparent phase accuracy while failing zero-matching admission; a real implementation must reject it.

## 1. A physical receiver with a universal variational guarantee

Let N:k -> D be any CPTP map, with normalized Choi state J=(id tensor N)(Phi_k).
The transpose below is on the KNOWN logical reference basis, not an unknown
physical basis. Put C=J^(T_R), a Hermitian operator on C^k tensor C^D.
For any unitary U on a FRESH logical k-register A and physical B-register, define

    R_U(X)=Tr_B[U(I_A/k tensor X)U*].                   (1)

This is CPTP on the entire carrier. No postselection, inverse source, output
support projection or learned coordinate frame occurs in its definition.

For source Kraus matrices K_l, write

    w_(l,a,b)=<b|K_l|a>,
    v_(l,a,b)=sum_i <i,b|U|a,K_l i>.

The receiver Kraus matrices are
L_(a,b)=(I_A tensor <b|)U(|a> tensor I_B)/sqrt(k). Thus

    F_e(R_U N)=sum_(l,a,b)|v_(l,a,b)|^2/k^3,
    Tr(U C)=sum_(l,a,b)conj(w_(l,a,b))v_(l,a,b)/k,
    sum_(l,a,b)|w_(l,a,b)|^2=k.

Cauchy gives the COMPLETE-channel lower bound

    F_e(R_U N)>=|Tr(U C)/k|^2.                        (2)

Conversely, for every CPTP recovery R, transpose on the untouched reference
commutes with R, and Phi_k^(T_R)=SWAP/k. Trace-norm contractivity on Hermitian
inputs therefore gives

    F_e(R N)<=||C||_1/k.                              (3)

Choose a unitary extension of sign(C), assigning any unit-modulus values on its
kernel. Then Tr[sign(C) C]=||C||_1. If F_opt=max_R F_e(RN),

    F_e(R_sign(C) N)>=(||C||_1/k)^2>=F_opt^2.         (4)

This is a different receiver from Petz in general. Squared-optimal recovery
guarantees themselves are established (Barnum--Knill, Tyson); generic polar
recovery is also established. C owns the strong primary comparison. Equation(4)+does not establish historical novelty or query optimality.

## 2. A gap-free unitary and actual-source tail

Use the globally unitary regularization

    U_c(C)=(C+i c I)(C^2+c^2 I)^(-1/2), c>0.          (5)

Its real variational objective is sum_j lambda_j^2/sqrt(lambda_j^2+c^2).
For each singular value s the loss from s is at most min(s,c).

Let A=N(I/k), and let tau be its spectral tail after the largest d0 eigenvalues.
Take P=I_k tensor P_top,d0 and Q=I-P. Since -I<=SWAP<=I and id tensor N is
positive,

    -I_k tensor A<=C<=I_k tensor A.

If -B<=X<=B with B>=0, its positive/negative spectral projectors give
Tr|X|<=TrB; this does NOT assert the generally false operator inequality |X|<=B.
Consequently ||Q C Q||_1<=k tau. Also C-QCQ has rank at most2kd0.
The best-rank trace-norm bound gives

    sum_(j>2kd0) s_j(C)<=k tau,
    ||C||_1-Re Tr(U_c C)<=2kd0 c+k tau.               (6)

Combining(2),(3),(6) yields

    F_e(R_Uc N)>=max(0,F_opt-2d0 c-tau)^2.

If F_opt>=1-kappa, a coarse all-range consequence is

    halfdiamond(R_Uc N,id_k)
        <=k sqrt(2kappa+4d0 c+2tau).                 (7)

The bound is allowed to be vacuous. With c=epsilon^2/(16 k^2 d0) and a complete
unitary-implementation half-diamond budget epsilon/2, triangle and square-root
subadditivity give epsilon+k sqrt(2kappa+2tau). Neither numerical kappa nor tau
is an algorithm input. d0 is a chosen complexity index. There is no exact-rank,
exact-isometry, nonzero source spectral gap, or unknown adjoint supplier.

# Extensive joint no-emission theorem via finite-support Lyapunov polynomials

**Status: constructive proof.** This establishes an extensive joint absence bound, not merely marginal mixing. It works for arbitrary positive g,kappa and arbitrary initial full-qubit states. Constants are catastrophically weak and do not establish the sharp weak-drive scaling c(D)g^2/kappa.

Model: full qubits, H=sum_z g X_z product_{y~z}(I-n_y), jumps sqrt(kappa)sigma^-_z, graph degree <=D. Let J_x^*(A)=kappa sigma_x^+ A sigma_x^-. For a marked set S define K_S=L^*-sum_{x in S}J_x^*. Then exp(tK_S)I is the effect of no emissions anywhere in S during [0,t]. These semigroups are completely positive and subunital.

## 1. Input: uniform local progress

The local-observability theorem gives, for every delta>0, a constant c=c(D,g,kappa,delta)>0 such that

 exp(delta K_{x})I <= (1-c)I

on every graph and for every x. The earlier proof was phrased on the independent-set subspace. IMPORTANT: to apply the product construction on the full tensor product, use its full-qubit extension: the same curvature estimate holds with a larger harmless constant, because Q L*²(n_x)Q=2g²G_xQ and the self-curvature on full qubits is 2g²G_x(1-2n_x). Its difference from 2g²G_x is bounded by 4g² n_x. Neighbor-count dissipative identities and all off-diagonal bounds are unchanged. Thus the same stated curvature constant and cutoff bound work on the full-qubit model too. No illegal-configuration loophole is present.

## 2. Finite local Taylor estimates

Put

 C0=4(g+kappa)(D+2)^2,
 delta=1/(4C0), q=C0 delta=1/4,
 a=(1-exp(-kappa delta))/kappa.

For K=K_{x}, locality and nested-generator counting give

 ||K^k I|| <= C0^k k!.

Proof: artificially include x in the support from the start. A nonzero Hamiltonian/dissipator term meets current support, and K has one additional local killing term at x. At most (D+3)|support| terms matter, each norm <=2(g+kappa), and support after j terms has size <=1+jD. The displayed C0 dominates the resulting product bound. Support radius grows at most two per term. The estimate is uniform in graph size.

Define the Hermitian finite-support polynomial

 F_x^(m)=sum_{k=0}^m delta^(k+1)/(k+1)! K_x^k(I).

It is supported in B_{2m}(x). Let F_x=integral_0^delta exp(sK_x)I ds. Bounded target intensity gives exp(sK_x)I>=exp(-kappa s)I, so

 aI <= F_x <= delta I.

The series bounds give

 ||F_x^(m)-F_x|| <= delta q^(m+1)/(1-q),
 ||K_x F_x^(m) - [exp(delta K_x)I-I]|| <= q^(m+2)/(1-q).

The second estimate follows EXACTLY by applying K to the polynomial and shifting its index; no extensive global generator norm is used.

Choose an integer m such that the first error <=a/2 and second error <=c/2. This choice depends only on D,g,kappa. Then

 (a/2)I <= F_x^(m) <= (3delta/2)I,
 K_x F_x^(m) <= -(c/2)I <= -r F_x^(m),
 r=c/(3delta)>0.

## 3. Buffered packing and product inequality

Given S, greedily choose S' subset S with pairwise center distances >4m+2. A degree bound gives

 |S'| >= |S|/B,
 B=(D+1)^(4m+3)

(a deliberately loose ball-volume bound). Write s=|S'| and F=product_{x in S'} F_x^(m). These positive factors have disjoint supports. The support of L^*(F_x^(m)) lies in B_{2m+2}(x), disjoint from every other factor's support by the chosen buffer.

The Hamiltonian obeys Leibniz, and each single-site dissipator acts on at most one factor. Therefore

 [L^*-sum_{x in S'}J_x^*]F
 =sum_{x in S'} [K_x F_x^(m)] product_{z!=x}F_z^(m)
 <= -rs F.

The ordering is valid because each local negative summand commutes with the remaining positive factors on disjoint supports. Additional killings x in S\S' subtract J_x^*(F)>=0, hence

 K_S F <= -rs F.

Positivity of the killed semigroup gives exp(tK_S)F<=exp(-rst)F. Using the bounds on F yields, for EVERY initial density matrix rho,

 P_rho[N_x(t)=0 for all x in S]
 <= (3delta/a)^s exp(-rst)
 <= C^|S| exp(-gamma |S| t),

 C=3delta/a,
 gamma=r/B=c/[3delta (D+1)^(4m+3)]>0.

The probability is also <=1, so take the minimum with one. Constants are independent of graph size, S, and rho.

## 4. Actual joint spacetime consequence

For nonoverlapping chronological time slabs j, with marked site sets S_j and durations T_j, the arbitrary-initial-state bound composes under conditioning on all preceding no-event records:

 P[every (x,j) with x in S_j has no event during slab j]
 <= product_j C^|S_j| exp[-gamma |S_j|T_j].

For a fixed slab length T this is a genuine local-stochastic upper bound p^(sum_j |S_j|), where p=C exp(-gamma T), whenever p<1. No independence assumption or multiplication of marginal bounds is used: each whole-slab marked-set event has its own extensive estimate.

## 5. What remains

This is a mathematically useful existence-level joint clock-stall law. Its rate gamma can be far smaller than g^2/kappa; obtaining gamma>=c(D)g^2/kappa with moderate C(D) remains open here. Also this theorem concerns the ideal clock only, not fault propagation under physical perturbations or a complete error-correction threshold.

# Independent audit of the extensive no-emission theorem

Auditor: joint-record-bound child worker, 2026-10-29.

## Verdict

No mathematical error found. The construction does establish an existence-level extensive same-slab absence estimate, and therefore a local-stochastic bound for arbitrary marked site/slab subsets on a chronological slab grid. It does not rely on an unjustified product of marginal probabilities or on mixing alone.

## Checked steps

### Full-qubit local-progress extension

On the full qubit space, the Hamiltonian off-diagonal observable in L*n_x is O_x=ig G_x(sigma-_x-sigma+_x), not the unguarded lowering operator. Its norm is at most g. The self-site double commutator is exactly 2g^2 G_x(1-2n_x). Subtracting 2g^2 G_x leaves a diagonal term whose expectation has magnitude at most 4g^2<f>. Neighboring Hamiltonian contributions remain x-off-diagonal, with each norm <=2g^2; all non-neighbor centers commute. Dissipators outside the closed star cancel, and the remaining dissipators preserve x-off-diagonality. Consequently the previously supplied loose curvature constant remains valid. Neighbor-count damping identities are also unchanged on the full tensor product. Thus the local-progress input really applies to arbitrary illegal/full-qubit configurations as claimed.

### Local Taylor counting

Artificially counting x in the support ensures the added killing term is always included. At most (D+3)|support| local terms are relevant, with individual norm <=2(g+kappa), and the support size after j applications is <=1+jD. This yields the safe coefficient base 2(g+kappa)(D+3)(D+1), which is less than C0=4(g+kappa)(D+2)^2. The k! bound follows. No global generator norm is hidden here.

The graph radius can grow by at most two per generator application because each guarded Hamiltonian is a star, whose diameter is two. Therefore F_x^(m) is indeed supported in B_{2m}(x).

### Polynomial and shifted residual

Applying K to F_m yields sum_{j=1}^{m+1}delta^j K^j(I)/j! EXACTLY. Thus its discrepancy from exp(delta K)I-I starts at j=m+2, not m+1. The geometric tail stated in the theorem is valid.

The survival operator lower bound exp(sK)I>=exp(-kappa s)I follows from a bounded target intensity, or directly from the differential trace inequality for the unnormalized no-target state. Hence aI<=F<=delta I. Approximation error <=a/2 implies a/2<=F_m<=3delta/2. The choice r=c/(3delta) correctly turns K F_m<=-(c/2)I into K F_m<=-rF_m.

### Exact product calculation

For selected centers separated by more than 4m+2, the support B_{2m+2}(x) of L*(F_x^(m)) is disjoint from B_{2m}(z) for every other selected center z. Hamiltonian commutators satisfy the Leibniz rule exactly. Each on-site damping term acts nontrivially on at most one factor, so its dissipative product correction vanishes. Each selected J_x acts only in its own factor. Thus the displayed product-generator identity is exact.

Each operator inequality K_x F_x^(m)<=-rF_x^(m) can be multiplied by the remaining positive factors because their supports commute with the entire local summand. The sum is therefore bounded by -rs F. For additional marked sites, J_x(F)>=0 follows from complete positivity and F>=0; no support or commutation condition is needed for this subtraction.

### Semigroup comparison and extensive exponent

For a positive semigroup, K_S F<=-rsF implies exp(tK_S)F<=exp(-rst)F by applying positivity to the Duhamel integral for K_S+rs. The lower and upper scalar bounds on the product F then give (3delta/a)^s exp(-rst).

The packing bound s>=|S|/B and s<=|S| imply

 (3delta/a)^s exp(-rst)
 <=(3delta/a)^|S| exp[-(r/B)|S|t],

because 3delta/a>=3>1. The degree-dependent ball-volume overestimate B=(D+1)^(4m+3) is safe, including D=0.

### Chronological slab conditioning

After conditioning on no-target emissions in all preceding slabs, the normalized current clock state is arbitrary. The extensive one-slab theorem applies to that state, so multiplying its conditional bounds is valid. This is not conditioning on simultaneous future records. Taking T large enough that C exp(-gamma T)<1 produces the stated product over marked site/slab cells.

## Scope cautions, not proof defects

- The theorem's constants can be extremely poor; no weak-drive-optimal gamma scaling follows.
- It treats the specified ideal Markovian clock. Physical error propagation, complementary auxiliary sectors, implementations, and a fault-tolerant computational threshold remain separate issues.
- The slab law is immediate on a common chronological grid. More general overlapping time windows require a reduction or separate argument and should not be silently included.
- An empty marked set has probability one, consistent with the exponent convention.
